title: Shimon ben Antiphras
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: It is told in Derekh Eretz Rabbah, beginning of chapter 6 (printed: רפ״ו), that they told Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai that he [Shimon ben Antiphras] would feed and give drink to all the guests who came to him, but at the time of their departure he would flog them. He [Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai] sent R' Yehoshua to him. When he arrived, he said to him, “Peace upon you, Rabbi.” He said to him, “I need a lodging.” He said to him, “Stay in peace.” They sat and engaged in Torah until evening. Afterward he escorted him (and did not flog him). He said to him, “Why have I heard about you that you flog the guests, yet you did not flog me?” He said to him, “Rabbi, you are a great sage and you have good manners. As for the people who come to me, I decreed that they should eat, but they vow by the Torah and transgress [their vows not to eat].” He said to him, “Blessed are you to Heaven for having done so.”[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The full narrative in [Derekh Eretz Rabbah 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Derekh_Eretz_Rabbah.6.1), the Hebrew Vilna 1883 edition, names Shimon ben Antipatros as the host and Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai as the recipient of the report. It supports the direction ‘they told’, the expansion of Hyman’s ריב״ז, and ‘beginning of chapter 6’ for רפ״ו. The heading’s spelling Antiphras is retained in the title; the parallel’s spelling is not silently substituted.

Hyman prints ור״א יש בך. The parallel instead has ודרך ארץ יש בידך, ‘you have good manners’. The English adopts that source-supported sense with this explicit notice of the different wording; Hyman’s Hebrew remains unchanged. The same complete parallel explains that the guests vowed not to eat or drink and then did so. The bracketed explanation of their broken vows supplies the ellipsis rather than inventing a prohibition.

This translates Hyman’s abridgment, including his parenthesis ‘and did not flog him’. Details present only in the longer parallel are not added to the narrative. ‘Stay in peace’ renders the lodging reply שב לשלום. These source comparisons establish the narrative sense, not an authority identity or independent endorsement of its historical claims.

The exact own Vilna paragraph has רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, supporting the full recipient title in this report. The two quoted uses of רבי in Hyman are retained as honorifics without supplying personal identities. His abbreviated ר׳ יהושע is represented as R' Yehoshua; no title is transferred from another occurrence.
